rv.q: It's one of the great performances of the season; to miss it would most definitely look like carelessness.
Each jewel of wit is polished apple-bright, and every performer is playing in the same key.
But then, Bedford's every line in this entertaining revival is a jewel.
His lips perpetually pursed as if sucking on a lemon, Bedford scowls and peers imperiously without ever betraying his real chromosomal makeup, even winkingly.
Bedford's lifetime commitment to the classics also accounts for the technically assured craftsmanship underpinning this lavishly mounted crowdpleaser.
There are worse things than spending quality time in such delightfully naughty company.
Highly stylized and sleekly staged, this is probably the funniest and sharpest production of the comedy, a favorite on regional and community stages, I've ever seen.
Under Bedford’s assured guidance, style is so vital in this Earnest that it all but sings.
This results in a brilliant performance that is just as hilarious as it is utterly convincing.
Yet 'Other Desert Cities' has the scent of truth about how families work, and don't work.

'The Importance of Being Earnest' turns 116 next month, and the old joker is surprisingly spry. Though the new Broadway revival of Oscar Wilde's satire isn't quite a nonstop delight -- it takes too long to rev up -- it makes for an enjoyable evening.
Roundabout’s revival of Oscar Wilde’s The Importance of Being Earnest is evidence that classics can weather the test of time.
This might not have been the best production of 'Earnest' I've ever seen, but it was accessible, pleasant and unexpectedly inventive.
